User wants proposal structure preserved up to design
claim: The requested workflow split keeps the current proposal structure through Description, Problem Statement, Goals, Non-Goals, Background, Viability, risks, and ADR metadata, while moving detailed design and architecture content out of proposal.md.
evidence: User clarification: keep the structure of proposal how it is now all the way up to design, including background and problem statement; original request moved design/architecture work to a new design doc phase.
relevance: Defines the central scope of this proposal.

title: User wants a requirements phase between proposal and design
claim: The requested workflow adds a phase between proposal and design that breaks accepted proposals into concrete product and behavioral requirements that drive design when the change impacts core user workflows or otherwise warrants a durable behavioral contract.
evidence: User request added requirements phase; later clarification: small changes that do not impact core user workflow do not need requirements.
relevance: Defines the new artifact layer and sequencing.

title: Existing proposal detail should be preserved but redistributed
claim: The existing proposal contents, construction method, detailed research, and non-design proposal sections should stay materially the same; detailed design/architecture output should move to requirements and design artifacts instead of remaining in proposal.md.
evidence: User request: contents, construction method, and detailed research should stay the same but split; later clarification: keep proposal structure as it is now all the way up to design, including Background and Problem Statement.
relevance: Prevents a scope interpretation that reduces research rigor or removes existing proposal quality gates.

title: OpenSpec separates source specs and change folders
claim: OpenSpec organizes repo-local work into specs/ as the source of truth for current behavior and changes/ as proposed modifications that contain artifacts and delta specs.
evidence: OpenSpec concepts: 'Specs are the source of truth' and 'Changes are proposed modifications' with repo-root/openspec/specs and changes folders.
relevance: Provides the external artifact model to mirror conceptually in Cartographer.

title: OpenSpec artifact flow is proposal to specs to design to tasks
claim: OpenSpec documents an artifact flow of proposal -> specs -> design -> tasks -> implement, where proposal captures intent/scope, specs capture what changes, design captures technical approach, and tasks capture implementation steps.
evidence: OpenSpec concepts Artifacts section and getting-started artifact table both describe proposal, specs, design, and tasks.
relevance: Matches the requested Cartographer phase split.

title: OpenSpec delta specs use ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED requirements
claim: OpenSpec delta specs describe behavior changes with ADDED Requirements, MODIFIED Requirements, and REMOVED Requirements sections, with scenarios under requirements.
evidence: OpenSpec concepts and getting-started docs show delta specs with ADDED, MODIFIED, REMOVED requirements and Given/When/Then scenarios.
relevance: Supplies a vocabulary for Cartographer-native requirements deltas.

title: OpenSpec specs are behavior contracts, not implementation plans
claim: OpenSpec describes specs as behavior contracts and says implementation details, class/function names, and step-by-step plans belong in design.md or tasks.md rather than specs.
evidence: OpenSpec concepts 'What a Spec Is (and Is Not)' section.
relevance: Supports keeping Cartographer requirements product/behavioral rather than design-heavy.

title: Current proposal workflow includes design in proposal.md
claim: The current Cartographer proposal workflow skeleton includes a ## Design section in proposal.md and instructs the planner to produce high-level implementation steps there.
evidence: skills/proposal/SKILL.md includes '## Design' in the proposal skeleton and later says to produce high-level implementation steps under ## Design.
relevance: Identifies the artifact coupling this proposal changes.

title: Current plan workflow owns plan.md and plan graph artifacts
claim: The current Cartographer planning workflow generates .plan/<topic>/plan.md plus plan.nodes.jsonl and plan.edges.jsonl for ordered phases, tasks, validations, and dependencies.
evidence: skills/plan/SKILL.md outputs list includes plan.md, plan.nodes.jsonl, and plan.edges.jsonl.
relevance: The new requirements/design phases must feed, not replace, existing plan graph generation.

title: Implementation keeps plan artifacts authoritative
claim: The implementation workflow treats .plan/<topic>/plan.md, plan.nodes.jsonl, plan.edges.jsonl, receipts.jsonl, and context-packs.jsonl as authoritative for planning, checkoff, validation history, and handoff context.
evidence: skills/implement/SKILL.md states these .plan artifacts remain authoritative during implementation.
relevance: Constrains the new requirements layer to add traceability without duplicating execution state.

title: Cartographer already validates proposal, fact, map, plan, receipt, and context-pack artifacts
claim: Cartographer's JSONL and planning graph validators read proposal.md, plan.md, map/fact JSONL, plan.nodes.jsonl, receipts.jsonl, and context-packs.jsonl to validate citations, private references, records, and graph integrity.
evidence: manage_jsonl.ts and validate_planning_graph.py read and validate the existing topic artifacts.
relevance: Adding requirements/design graph validation should extend existing validation surfaces instead of inventing a separate validator stack.

title: OpenSpec should be compatibility inspiration, not a hard dependency
claim: The user-supplied research recommends borrowing OpenSpec's artifact model and supporting OpenSpec-compatible import/export adapters, while keeping Cartographer's graph structures, receipts, audits, and decay model as the internal source of truth.
evidence: Research session: 'do not fold OpenSpec in as a hard dependency' and 'OpenSpec-compatible, not OpenSpec-dependent.'
relevance: Sets the interoperability strategy for this proposal.

title: Graph-backed requirements can participate in traceability and decay
claim: A Cartographer-native requirements layer should use stable IDs and graph edges so requirements can link to facts, proposal goals, design nodes, plan tasks, validations, receipts, changed files, audits, and decay analysis.
evidence: User-supplied research recommends requirements.nodes.jsonl and requirements.edges.jsonl with fields such as sources, validated_by, implemented_by, and status.
relevance: Defines why requirements.md should be a projection over graph records rather than just prose.

title: Artifact proliferation risk
claim: Adding requirements and design artifacts can increase workflow ceremony and maintenance burden if validation and docs do not make their boundaries obvious.
evidence: Derived from current workflow adding new mandatory artifact types to existing proposal/plan/implement surfaces.
relevance: Must be mitigated with progressive rigor, concise lightweight proposal output, and graph summaries.

title: Traceability drift risk
claim: Splitting proposal, requirements, design, and plan artifacts creates a risk that statements, IDs, and validations drift unless cross-artifact edges and validators are introduced with the split.
evidence: Derived from Cartographer's existing reliance on JSONL citation and endpoint validation.
relevance: Drives requirements.edges.jsonl, design graph references, and validator updates.

title: Do not reduce research rigor
claim: The split must keep current proposal research and evidence gathering rigor; it changes artifact boundaries, not evidence standards.
evidence: Supported by F003.
relevance: Design and implementation must preserve fact graphs, map graphs, receipts, and audit gates.

title: Cartographer topic maps to OpenSpec change and folds requirement deltas into docs requirements
claim: In the proposed workflow, a Cartographer topic is equivalent to an OpenSpec change: topic-local requirements are deltas for that change, and after implementation/archive those deltas should be folded into durable project requirements under docs/requirements.md, with multiple requirements files allowed if the permanent document becomes too long.
evidence: User clarification: our "topic" = "change" in OpenSpec, follow the same development cycle, keep one docs/requirements.md like docs/adr, and specs in the topic/change are deltas that get folded into permanent docs/requirements.
relevance: Defines the lifecycle and durable location for accepted behavioral requirements.

title: Design should be graph-backed from the start
claim: The design phase should include design.nodes.jsonl and design.edges.jsonl from the first implementation for scoped changes that warrant requirements, because structured references from design decisions to requirements are valuable and Cartographer already uses the Markdown plus JSONL graph pattern for plans.
evidence: User clarification: add JSONL for design; structured data references to requirements are too valuable to pass up and the plan workflow already has that pattern.
relevance: Resolves the previous open question about Markdown-only design by requiring graph-backed design artifacts.

title: OpenSpec workflows documentation
OpenSpec commands documentation
OpenSpec CLI documentation
OpenSpec customization documentation
OpenSpec current lifecycle includes verify, sync, and archive
claim: Current OpenSpec docs describe a completion lifecycle where implementation can be verified against artifacts, delta specs can be synced into main specs, and archive validates then merges specs and moves the change to a dated archive folder.
evidence: OpenSpec workflows and commands docs describe /opsx:verify, /opsx:sync, /opsx:archive, and CLI openspec archive validating, merging delta specs into openspec/specs, and moving changes to archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>.
relevance: Cartographer should mirror the lifecycle with verify/fold/archive concepts while adding receipts and graph validation.

title: OpenSpec supports agent-readable status, validation, and schema-driven artifacts
claim: OpenSpec CLI supports JSON output for list, show, validate, status, instructions, templates, schemas, and change metadata commands, and its schemas define artifact IDs, generated paths, templates, instructions, dependencies, and apply requirements.
evidence: OpenSpec CLI docs list agent-compatible commands and schema fields; customization docs define schema.yaml artifacts with id, generates, template, instruction, requires, and apply.tracks.
relevance: No obvious blocker exists for a later adapter if Cartographer stores equivalent metadata and stable graph IDs.

title: OpenSpec import/export mapping needs domains, scenarios, change types, and archive metadata
claim: A future OpenSpec adapter should preserve domains, requirement/scenario structure, ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED and current RENAMED-style sync change types, proposal/design/tasks equivalents, schema metadata, validation status, and archive history.
evidence: OpenSpec docs describe specs by domain, requirement/scenario format, ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED deltas, /opsx:sync parsing ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED/RENAMED sections, proposal/specs/design/tasks artifacts, schemas, validate/status JSON, and archive folders.
relevance: Defines what Cartographer must not omit now if later import/export should be straightforward.

title: Small non-core changes do not require requirements artifacts
claim: Small changes that do not impact a core user workflow do not need requirements or design graph artifacts by default; requirements should be required by scope/risk of change, similar to ADR gating.
evidence: User clarification: "Small changes that don't impact core user workflow don't need reqs."
relevance: Defines the scope gate for when the new requirements/design phase is mandatory.

title: Design graph MVP uses decision and alternative schema
claim: The first design graph schema should implement the Decision + Alternative model with design-decision, design-alternative, design-component, and design-risk nodes plus core traceability edges; full implementation traceability should be documented as a fast-follow.
evidence: User agreed to option B first and to document option C as fast follow.
relevance: Resolves the minimum design JSONL schema open question for first implementation.
